unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'Fit it yourself.' and 'replace the relay/overload kit' recommended without any test confirming the relay, after the shake test was inconclusive.

rationale: The assistant correctly identified the start relay/overload as the likely cause and kept the customer's unplugged checks safe. However, it relied on an unreliable shake test and repeated it across turns. It then pushed the customer to buy and fit the part without engineer confirmation or a continuity test, and overstated confidence ('statistically most likely', 'well within your budget') with no real price given. It did not answer the part-number or cost questions, and it left out the condenser cleaning and the advice to have an engineer confirm before buying parts.
